newsitem.title: USA: Demand, rates rope US corp issuers into debt arena.
newsitem.headline: Demand, rates rope US corp issuers into debt arena.

text.p: Buyside demand coupled with a favorable rate environment continues to lure U.S. corporations into the debt arena, traders said.
"The demand continues to be there for corporate paper and with (Treasury) yields at these levels it's a favorable time for issuers to bring debt to market," said one high-grade syndicate source.
Players said Caterpillar Inc's upcoming $300 million 100-year bond issue is already issue-bid going into the pricing, which is expected later today.
Current price talk on the issue is in the low 70 basis points area, sources said. The deal, which will be underwritten by Merrill Lynch & Co, is callable after 50 years.
Another deal expected to price this week is Chrysler Corp's $600 million A3/A-minus rated 30-year debt offering, via Salomon Brothers Inc.
The deal is expected to consist of an A3/A-minus rated 30-year issue with price talk in the area of 68 to 70 basis points over Treasuries, sources said.
Southwest Airlines' upcoming $100 million debt offering via Lehman Brothers is said to also be issue-bid on the street, syndicate sources said.
The A3/A-minus rated 30-year debt issue is expected to carry a make-whole call at 20 basis points over U.S. Treasuries, sources said.
In addition, Seagate Technology Inc is expected to issue a three-part Baa3/BBB rated $750 million debt offering on Tuesday, via Morgan Stanley & Co, sources said.
The deal is expected to consist of seven-year, 10-year and 40-year, puttable in 12th year, maturities, sources said.
Turning to the private placement sector, Revlon Worldwide Corp is getting set to issue $500 million in 10-year senior discount notes on Friday via Chase Securities Inc.
The new issue is expected to have a four-year zero coupon, sources added.
Also, Enterprise Rent-A-Car is gearing up to tap the corporate bond new issue market with a $250 million 144A private placement debt offering via Goldman Sachs & Co.
The offering consist of a seven-year issue, sources added.
